title: Counter programs preserve unary logspace
statement: Let $R\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Lambda$ be a finite set with decidable equality, and let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$, with initial label $\ell_0$. Suppose $u,g:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}^*$, and both the bit-membership and output-length languages associated to $u$ are decidable in logarithmic space. If there are natural numbers $C,c$ such that, for every $n$, the program on input $u(n)$ halts within $C(n+1)^c$ steps and has output $g(n)$, then both corresponding languages for $g$ are decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: Finite label set $\Lambda$ with decidable equality
Functions $u,g$ from naturals to finite bit strings
